text: All patient health information, including electronic medical records, diagnostic images, and laboratory results, shall be encrypted using AES-256 encryption in transit over HTTPS/TLS 1.3 and at rest in the database, with cryptographic keys managed through a hardware security module (HSM) compliant with FIPS 140-2 Level 3 standards and rotated annually, ensuring confidentiality of protected health information across the entire IT infrastructure.
label: Security

text: The healthcare information system shall maintain comprehensive audit logs capturing user login attempts, data access events, modifications to patient records, system configuration changes, and privilege escalations with timestamps in UTC, user identifiers, action descriptions, and outcomes, retaining these logs for a minimum of seven years to support HIPAA compliance, breach investigations, and forensic analysis as required by healthcare regulatory frameworks.
label: Security

text: User sessions accessing patient data shall automatically terminate after fifteen minutes of inactivity, require re-authentication upon session resumption, and limit concurrent sessions per user to three active connections maximum, with the system logging all session lifecycle events and alerting security teams to suspicious patterns such as simultaneous logins from geographically disparate locations within the healthcare facility's IT operations center.
label: Security

text: The system shall validate and sanitize all user inputs, including clinical notes, search queries, file uploads, and HL7/FHIR API requests, to prevent injection attacks, cross-site scripting (XSS), and malicious code execution, implementing parameterized queries for database access and maintaining a whitelist of allowable file types and maximum file sizes for diagnostic image and document uploads within the healthcare infrastructure.
label: Security

text: De-identification and data minimization controls shall ensure that healthcare staff access only the minimum necessary patient attributes required for their clinical or administrative function, with algorithms automatically redacting sensitive identifiers such as social security numbers, addresses, and phone numbers from default record displays, and requiring explicit justification and supervisor approval for access to complete unredacted patient profiles.

text: The healthcare information system shall enforce encrypted data transmission to all connected clinical devices, hospital information systems, pharmacy systems, laboratory systems, and external healthcare providers using mutual TLS authentication with certificate validation, supporting only cryptographically-strong protocols (TLS 1.2 minimum, preferably TLS 1.3), and maintaining a registry of all connected external systems with documented security assessments and integration contracts that specify data protection requirements.
label: Security

text: All database backup files containing patient health information shall be encrypted using AES-256, stored on geographically-separated secure servers, replicated daily with recovery point objective (RPO) of four hours and recovery time objective (RTO) of two hours, and restored to isolated environments quarterly to verify backup integrity and business continuity procedures, with backups retained according to the healthcare organization's records retention policy aligned with HIPAA minimum requirements.
label: Security

text: The system shall implement real-time intrusion detection and prevention capabilities monitoring for suspicious database queries, unusual data access patterns, brute-force authentication attempts, and anomalous system behavior, utilizing machine learning algorithms trained on healthcare IT environments, with automated response actions blocking identified threats and escalating alerts to security personnel through the healthcare facility's security operations center.

text: Healthcare providers and administrative users shall be required to complete HIPAA privacy and security awareness training upon hire and annually thereafter, with demonstrated understanding through assessment, and role-specific training on secure handling of patient data, incident reporting procedures, and appropriate use of healthcare IT systems, with training completion records maintained in the healthcare organization's compliance management system and reviewed during internal audits.

text: The healthcare information system shall prevent the download or export of unencrypted patient data to removable media devices, personal computers, or cloud storage services, implementing data loss prevention (DLP) controls that scan outbound network traffic, enforce mandatory encryption for any approved data transfers, and maintain audit trails of all data export requests including requestor identity, data elements requested, export destination, and business justification.

text: Password policies for healthcare staff shall require minimum fourteen characters, complexity requirements including uppercase and lowercase letters, numeric and special characters, prohibit reuse of previous eight passwords, enforce expiration every ninety days, and lock accounts after six failed authentication attempts for thirty minutes, with single sign-on (SSO) capabilities using Active Directory or LDAP to reduce password fatigue while maintaining security standards across the integrated healthcare IT environment.

text: The system shall integrate with the healthcare facility's vulnerability management program, undergoing quarterly penetration testing by accredited security professionals against HIPAA Security Rule requirements, with documented remediation of identified weaknesses within defined timeframes based on severity classifications, and annual comprehensive security risk assessments reviewing controls effectiveness, emerging threats, and alignment with healthcare industry security standards.

text: The Fleet Management System shall implement anomaly detection for fleet vehicle telemetry data streams, establishing baseline behavioral profiles for each vehicle including speed patterns, location boundaries, and engine diagnostics, flagging deviations exceeding two standard deviations as potential GPS spoofing or sensor tampering, with alerts generated within 30 seconds and logged to a security information and event management (SIEM) system.

text: The Fleet Management System shall enforce secure password management for developer accounts through integration with a centralized secrets management system, requiring developers to retrieve database credentials on-demand with 1-hour validity periods, implementing automatic credential revocation upon session termination, and maintaining an audit trail of all credential access attempts with notification to security operations within 5 minutes of anomalous patterns.

text: API endpoints for fleet telematics data access shall implement request signing using HMAC-SHA256 with a shared secret key rotated every 90 days, requiring API clients to include a cryptographic timestamp in requests valid only within a 5-minute window to prevent replay attacks, with request signatures validated server-side before processing and signature verification failures logged with client IP address and attempted payload hash.

text: The Fleet Management System shall deploy intrusion detection system (IDS) sensors on all production networks hosting vehicle data processing services, monitoring for indicators of compromise including unauthorized outbound connections, abnormal protocol traffic patterns, and suspicious internal lateral movement, with detection sensitivity configured to alert on any traffic to known malicious IP addresses updated daily, and alerts correlated with firewall logs for comprehensive threat investigation.
